title: perf(desktop): cut the wait before a recording starts
body:
## Summary

Since record modes (#384), every "Start recording" opens the capture overlay first, and starting a take feels much slower. This PR removes the waits that a read-only audit found on the start path, and adds permanent `[record-timing]` log lines so the remaining time can be measured instead of guessed.

**Stacks on #391** (`fix/countdown-wait-for-shade`, not merged yet). It is based on that branch and uses its `recording:countdown-visible` handshake. Merge #391 first. Until then this diff also shows #391's commit.

All gains below are **estimates from reading the code**. Nothing was measured in Electron. The timing lines exist so the next step can use real numbers.

## What each commit removes from the start path

| Commit | Removed from the start path | Estimated gain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chore(desktop): log [record-timing] marks…` | Nothing. Adds one log line per step (see below). | — |
| `perf(desktop): open the countdown shade with the region and keep screen sources listed` | (1) `desktopCapturer.getSources` after the overlay closes, while nothing is on screen. The sources are now listed when the overlay opens and kept until a display changes (`ScreenSourceCache`). (2) Creating the shade only on the recorder's first tick report. `prepareRegionCountdown` now opens the shade itself, painted with "3", so it loads while the start request reaches the recorder. #391 still holds: the clock starts only once the shade is on screen. A tick report now only repaints the shade and can no longer count as "visible". | 0.1–0.5 s from the source listing, plus 50–300 ms from the shade starting earlier. This shortens the blank gap between the overlay closing and "3" appearing. |
| `perf(desktop): keep the next capture overlay loaded hidden` | Creating one `BrowserWindow` per display and loading the full renderer into each at every pick. The windows for the most likely next pick are now loaded hidden: 3 s after launch, and 2 s after each pick ends (held off while a take is pending or running). A pick whose queries match these hidden windows exactly shows them at once. Any other pick throws them away and loads its own windows, as it does today. | 0.3–1 s before the overlay shows, on a matching pick |
| `perf(desktop): open the mic with the screen and take the poster frame off the start` | (1) The mic `getUserMedia` waiting for the screen stream, the frame-size measure and the compositor; it now opens at the same time as the screen. (2) The engine handle waiting for the poster thumbnail (play + fixed 150 ms + `toBlob`); the thumbnail is now taken in the background and `stop` waits up to 1 s for it. (3) `setLoginItemSettings`, re-registering every global shortcut, and rebuilding the tray menu on every settings write (each mode change). | ~150–300 ms of thumbnail time, plus the mic open time (tens to a few hundred ms), plus a few ms per mode change |

### Design notes on the hidden overlay windows (the riskiest commit)
- **No window is reused.** Each hidden window is fresh and serves one pick, then it is destroyed as before. The renderer's per-pick React state (answered flag, frame box, intent) therefore never carries over from one pick to the next.
- **Which windows are loaded:** the intent of the last pick (record before any pick) in that intent's remembered mode. Nothing is loaded when that pick would show no overlay: Screen on a single display, or a mode that is switched off (Window, NIW2-469).
- **When they are thrown away and reloaded:** on `display-added`, `display-removed` and `display-metrics-changed`; on a change to the recording or screenshot mode, the language or the theme; and when one crashes or fails to load.
- **ADR 0029:** the windows are still `panel`s. A hidden window never calls `setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces`; that still happens only when it is shown, with `skipTransformProcessType`. Covered by a test.
- **Cost:** one hidden renderer per display stays in memory between picks. The Capture Panel already follows the same pre-load pattern.

### Not changed, on purpose
- **Cancel and stop paths** are left alone because they are being fixed in parallel: `beginEngine` cancel handling, `bar.show` after stop, `showMainWindow` on an abandoned countdown, and the play timeouts in the compositor and thumbnail. This PR touches `captureThumbnail` only at its call site (not its body), and changes one line of `stopRecording` (the thumbnail is now awaited as a promise).
- **The Window mode thumbnail picker** (`recording-sources.ts`, `getSources` with thumbnails, 0.5–2 s) is unchanged. Window has no overlay picker while NIW2-469 keeps it off.
- **`measureFrameSize`** is unchanged. It normally costs about one frame, and its `[record-timing]` line will show whether that is true.

## How to read `[record-timing]`

Main prints one line per step to its stdout (the terminal running `bun run dev`; for a packaged build, launch `Kaipu Record.app/Contents/MacOS/Kaipu Record` from a terminal):

```
[record-timing] +0ms start clicked (last mode)
[record-timing] +412ms overlay shown on display 1
[record-timing] +2310ms overlay answered (record)
[record-timing] +2311ms selectArea: resolving the screen source
[record-timing] +2312ms selectArea: screen source resolved
[record-timing] +2313ms start request sent to the recorder
[record-timing] +2318ms renderer: requestStartRecording
[record-timing] +2540ms countdown shade shown
[record-timing] +2541ms renderer: countdown visible, clock started
[record-timing] +5544ms renderer: beginEngine
...
[record-timing] +5790ms renderer: status recording
```
(The numbers above are illustrative, not measured.)

- `+Nms` counts from the click that began the timeline. For a start, that is the Start click or shortcut. For a stop, the timeline restarts at `renderer: stop requested`.
- Lines marked `renderer:` come from the recorder. They are forwarded to main and printed on main's clock, so the terminal shows one timeline. The recorder's DevTools console also prints them, counted from its own first mark.
- The 3-second countdown sits between `countdown visible` and `beginEngine`. The **time the user waits** is the gaps on either side of it: from the click to the overlay shown, from the overlay answer to the shade shown, and from `beginEngine` to `status recording`.
- No line is printed outside an open timeline, so screenshots and idle time stay quiet.

## Tests

- `bun run check-types`: clean.
- `bunx oxlint src`: 0 errors (17 existing warnings, none in the changed files).
- `bunx vitest run` in `apps/kaipu-record`: 283 files, 2603 tests passing.
- New or changed tests:
  - `record-timing.test.ts`
  - `screen-source-cache.test.ts`
  - hub: the shade opens on "3" when the region is prepared; a tick that arrives while the shade loads does not count as visible; one listing serves a prefetch and the pick; a display change lists again
  - overlay hidden windows: 9 cases, including hidden-until-pick (ADR 0029), a matching pick showing them at once, a mismatched pick, waiting while busy, display change, crash
  - engine: the mic opens alongside the screen; the mic is released when the screen fails; the start does not wait for the poster frame
  - settings: the login item is set only on change; keyed listeners

## QA (owner)

Please run a dev build from a terminal and paste the `[record-timing]` lines for:
1. **Frame**: one start (Start recording → draw or keep the frame → Record), then one stop after a few seconds.
2. **Screen**: one start and one stop. With one display, Screen skips the overlay.
3. The second start of a session, Frame again. This is the case where the overlay should show almost at once, because its windows were loaded hidden.

While doing that, check:
- The countdown still reads a full **3**, 2, 1 on the chosen region, and no 3 is cut short (#391).
- Esc during the countdown still cancels it and brings the app back.
- The overlay looks right on its first frame: correct mode, correct intent (Record), and the frame where you left it, including after changing the mode chip, the language, or plugging in or unplugging a display.
- The mic is in the recording, and the light turns off after stop.
- The library thumbnail of the new take is present.
- The app stays in the Dock and in ⌘-Tab while the overlay is used (ADR 0029).
